Culpable

/KUL-puh-bul/ — rhymes with bull · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Culpable describes someone who deserves blame for having done something wrong.

The inspector found the factory culpable for the polluted river.

Worked Example

An oil company ignored environmental warnings and spilled toxic waste into the sea — they were culpable for the ecological disaster.

Culpable means deserving blame for wrongdoing. It's more specific than just 'responsible' because it clearly assigns moral or legal fault for doing something wrong, not merely being involved in a cause.

How Culpable Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

responsible

responsible: answerable for something because it was your doing

guilty

guilty: having actually committed the wrong or crime

blameworthy

blameworthy: deserving to be blamed or criticized

Antonyms

innocent

innocent: having done nothing wrong at all

blameless

blameless: completely free of any fault or blame

How Strong Is It? — innocent → responsible → guilty → culpable

innocent vs. culpable

innocent vs. culpable: Innocent sits at the opposite end of the scale from culpable: an innocent person deserves no blame at all, while a culpable one has clearly earned it.

responsible vs. culpable

responsible vs. culpable: Responsible is weaker than culpable — being responsible only means something was your job or your doing, while culpable adds the harsher judgment that you deserve blame for a wrong.

guilty vs. culpable

guilty vs. culpable: Guilty is strong, but culpable pushes one step further on this scale — guilty says you committed the wrong, while culpable stresses that you fully deserve the blame and its consequences.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — culp(a)

Root — culp(a): blame, fault (Latin)

Suffix — -able

Suffix — -able: deserving of, worthy of (Latin (-abilis))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin culpa means 'blame or fault,' and the suffix -able means 'deserving of' — put together, culpable literally means 'deserving of blame,' which is exactly what the word still means today.

Use the root in a new word: culprit

Use the root in a new word: culprit: The detective finally named the culprit — the person whose fault the crime was — a word built on the very same Latin root culpa, 'blame,' that hides inside culpable.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / legal

Culpable is the word for serious legal or moral fault — when someone deserves blame for wrongdoing. For general responsibility or involvement without blame, use 'responsible.' Reserve culpable for situations where fault is the key point.
